about: Who a call through a register may reach, for the stack bound of the fixed-memory images (scripts/lib/stack_bound_gate.py, docs/text-ownership.md). A register can hold only an address the image holds somewhere (a data word, a literal pool, a movw/movt pair, an adr), so a rule names, among those functions, the ones its site may call. Every call by register in a function the bound reaches needs a rule; there is no reading of the vtable slot or of the method named on the line. `where` is a source file (the end of its path) and one of: nothing more (every call by register of the file, whose number the image pins in `site_pins`); `anchor`, a fragment of the source of the line the call is on (it follows the call when lines are added above it, and the contract check fails when no line of the file holds it); `line` with `library`, a position in a file this repository does not hold, which is a fact of one version of it and so names the library, pinned to its commit in `libraries` (the compiler's core library at the toolchain's commit; a site of another commit is not claimed and the gate says so); or `function`, a regex on the demangled name of the function that makes the call (for C, on its name). A position in a file of this repository is refused. `callees` is a regex on the demangled name without generic arguments, or WAKER (the four functions of the executor's RawWakerVTable, read from the image), or TRAIT_METHODS (every trait-impl method the image holds, for a site that is shallow), or NONE. A NONE rule states a premise, and `absent` (a regex on the functions the image holds an address of) or `absent_reached` (on the functions the bound reaches) is that premise: the gate fails when it stops being true. A rule is written by a person and read against the code; the gate holds it to the image.

thread_entry.why: the main thread's stack holds, beneath wz_app_main, the kernel's frames that run it (z_thread_entry, bg_thread_main and the app's main: 56 bytes in the images) and, at the top of the stack, the thread-local storage and the alignment (16 bytes with the 8 of .tbss). Read off the real stack of the plain client on the kit by walking its frame-pointer chain at the deepest write (2026-11-03): wz_app_main's entry was 72 bytes deep, and the bound that started at wz_app_main was 16 bytes under the kit's reading

recursion.why: a slot's release drops what the slot holds, which holds a handle to another slot: the session's slot inside the pump's cell, two or three deep

a call of the `Fn` the send's dispatch was handed (`as_encoder`, a trait object), made in the dispatch and in the frame writer under it that a batching window uses: the closure of `send_response_final`, of `dispatch_declare_lent` or of `send_reply_parts`, each written at the call that sends and passed by reference for the length of it. The rule is the call's own place in the library (`core::ops::function`) and not the function that makes it, so the calls through a `TxBuf` that sit in the same functions stay the rules of `tx_buf.rs` below; its number of sites is pinned for each image, so another call through a `Fn` is read before it is claimed

the entry walk, the effective targets and the final-state test take the document's tables, the store and sets, and no Behaviour (microstep.rs, `walk_entry`, `effective_target_states_on`, `is_in_final_state`): their calls through a register are the history and parallel procedures read from the tables (`HISTORY` and `PARALLEL`), which a document without a <history> and a <parallel> does not carry, so none is linked (the premise: no function of the image is one of the seven procedures of the two tables). The Behaviour hooks are called from `enter_states`, beside them and not under them, and the rule below claims them there

the asks of the machine the engine drives (its host, behind a reference to MainLoop), made by `Turn::run` (the entry into the initial configuration and the main event loop it hands over to). `Turn` holds the machine as a `&mut dyn MainLoop` (engine.rs `struct Turn`), and its `core`, `behaviour`, `queue` and `start_pending_invokes` are the methods of that trait. The rule claims by the function and stands BEFORE the rules that claim by file: the file a line table gives a register call inside `Turn::run` is not the same in every build (the lab host, a workstation and the hosted runner gave three splits of the same sites among `engine-host`, this rule and `engine-behaviour`), and a count that depends on it is a pin that goes red on a machine that did not move it
